title: GA/64/2014 of State Of Uttarakhand Vs Teetu Alias Suresh

paras.text:
1
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Government Appeal No. 64 of 2014
State of Uttarakhand ..................Appellant

-Versus-Teetu alias Suresh .............Respondent
Present: Mr. J. S. Virk, learned Deputy Advocate General for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Rajeev Kumar Sharma, learned Amicus Curiae for the respondent.
Date of Hearing and Order: 15.11.2022
Coram:-
Shri Sanjaya Kumar Mishra, J.
Shri Alok Kumar Verma, J.
Upon hearing the learned counsel for the parties, the Court has
passed the following order:-
1. The State of Uttarakhand, in this appeal against
acquittal, has assailed the acquittal of the respondent -
Teetu @ Suresh S/o Shri Karan Singh, who has been
acquitted by the VIIth Additional Session Judge, District
- Dehradun in Session Trial No. 18 of 2007 as per the
judgment dated 12.02.2014. The respondent was facing
trial for commission of offence under Sections 328 &
302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred
to as "the Penal Code" for brevity).
2. The case of the prosecution, in short, is that the
deceased happens to be daughter of Vikram Singh, the

2
complainant in this case. The complainant had four
children, out of whom, Sheetal was about 15 to 16 years
of age at the time of occurrence.
3. On 15.04.2006, in the night, she came in
staggering/unstable condition 1⁄4yM +[kM +krs gq,1⁄2 to her house
and described before her parents that the respondent
i.e. Teetu, who is the son of Karan Singh, was having
love affairs with the deceased and that has promised the
deceased to marry her. In the meantime, his marriage
was fixed with some other person, when the deceased
protested the same, the respondent told her that they
cannot live together but they can die together, and
therefore, he called her to the backside of her house in
agriculture field and took out a bottle, with poison in it
and stated that both of them should drink the same and
should die. Thereafter, the respondent made her drink
poison from the bottle but when Sheetal asked him to
drink poison from the bottle, the respondent adopted
delaying tactics and he left the deceased there. The
deceased came to her house and described the incident
before her parents and then she became unconscious.
Thereafter, she was taken to the government hospital,

3
where, she was referred to the Jolly Grant Hospital, after
some time in the hospital, she died.
4. Describing these facts, the PW-5 - complainant of the
case submitted a written F.I.R. before the S.H.O.
Doiwala, Dehradun, and therefore, the criminal case no.
54 of 2006 was registered under Section 328 & 302 of
the Penal Code against the respondent - Teetu @
Suresh.
5. On 16.04.2006, upon the investigation, the Investigating
Officer held inquest on the dead body of the deceased
and dispatched the same for post-mortem examination.
After post mortem examination, he received the post-mortem examination report. He examined the witnesses
and recorded their statements, visited the spot. He also
dispersed the visceras of the deceased for Chemical and
Serological examination. Upon completion of
investigation, he submitted charge-sheet against the
respondent. The defence took the plea of denial in this
case.
6. In order to prove its case, the prosecution has
examined 08 witnesses, out of whom, PW-5 Vikram

4
Singh is the complainant of the case. He and PW - 1
Smt. Kanta, mother of the deceased have stated
about the oral dying declaration made by the
deceased in the fateful night. PW - 3 Pawan Kumar
(brother of the deceased) has also stated about the
dying declaration. PW - 2 Dr. Gyanendra Singh
Rawat had conducted post-mortem examination on
the dead body of the deceased and the rest of the
witnesses are either formal witnesses or official
witnesses. PW - 6 Chaman Lal is a witness to the
respondent and the deceased going together, but he
has not supported the prosecution, and has been
declared hostile.
7. The examination of the statement of PW - 2 Dr.
Gyanendra Singh Rawat reveals that there is only
one injury on the right knee, which was stated to be
abrasion of the size 1 x 1 cm, which could have been
caused by rubbing against ground. He has further
stated that as per the post-mortem examination and
as per the report of the Himalayan hospital, death
could have been caused because of poisoning due to
the consumption of Aluminum Phosphide. He

5
collected the contents of the stomach and visceras
like a piece of intestine, pieces of lever, spline and
kidney, which were sent for chemical examination.
The chemical examination reveals that the said
poison Aluminum Phosphide was found in the
visceras. Thus, it is clear that the death of the
deceased was definite due to poisoning.
8. Now, the question arises whether the learned
Additional Session Judge was right in acquitting the
respondent, in view of the evidences available on
record. It is not disputed at this stage that the dying
declaration, which was not accepted by the learned
Additional Session Judge, was made orally by the
deceased before her parents and brother. At that
time, no medical expert was present to certify the
mental capacity of the deceased.
9. It is also borne out from the record that she was in a
very unstable/staggering state 1⁄4yM+[kM+kr s gq, vkbZ1⁄2, in the
sense that she was unable to walk properly.

6
10. In this connection, we have to examine the
statement of PW - 5, who is the father of the
deceased as well as the complainant of the case. He
has stated on oath that he had four children, out of
whom, Sheetal was his daughter. He has stated on
oath that on 15.04.2006, the witness - Smt. Kanta,
mother of the deceased returned at 8:30 pm from
the agriculture field after harvesting feed crops, at
that time, Sheetal was in the house. After taking
meal at about 9 to 9:30 pm, Sheetal went outside at
9:30 pm for washing utensils. After one or two
minutes, she came in a wavering/unstable condition
1⁄4yM+[kM+kr s gq, ?kj okil vkbZ1⁄2. And then on their asking in the
presence of his wife Kanta PW - 1, the deceased
stated that Teetu and herself, wherein involved with
each other in a love affair but Teetu's marriage was
fixed with some other person. Therefore, the witness
further stated that the deceased revealed before him
that respondent - Teetu called her and stated that
they cannot live together in their lifetime but they
can die together. Thereafter, the witness stated that
the deceased further revealed that Teetu took out a

7
bottle and made her drink poisonous out of the
same but he himself did not drink poison and
resorted to dilly-dallying and after some time, he left
her on that place. Then, she came to her house and
stated about the incident.
11. The evidence of PW - 5 receives corroboration from
the statement of PW - 1, who has stated that on that
day after taking food, Sheetal went outside for
washing the utensils. Thereafter, she left the
utensils in the house and went towards the field for
attending call of nature. About 1 to 2 minutes
thereafter, she came in a wavering/unstable
condition, at that time, it was 10:00 pm. When the
witness asked her what happened, she revealed that
she was having love affairs with the respondent -
Teetu. Thereafter, the deceased told the witness that
he is going to marry somebody else, on which, the
respondent - Teetu stated that they cannot live
together but they can die together, then he took out
a bottle and made her drink poisonous but he did

8
not drink it himself and adopted dilly-dallying
tactics. Thereafter, he left the place.
12. It is borne out from the record that her brother has
been examined as PW - 3. PW - 3 Pawan Kumar has
stated that when she came back to her house in a
wavering / unstable condition at that time, his
parents asked her, then the deceased revealed before
her parents that there was a love relationship
between Teetu and herself and that he told her that
she will drink the poison and thereafter, he will
drink poison because he was get married to some
other person. Thereafter, respondent - Teetu
administered poison to her but did not consume the
same himself and left her in that place.
13. The principle of law is no more Res-Integra, as far as
dying declaration is concerned. The Hon'ble
Supreme Court, in many cases, has held that dying
declaration can be accepted as the sole material
available for recording the conviction of the
respondent. In the case of "Smt. Paniben Vs. State of

9
Gujarat: (1992) 2 SCC 474" the Hon'ble Supreme
Court has held that though, a dying declaration is
entitled to a great weight, it is worthwhile to note that
accused has no power of cross examination. Such a
power is essential for eliciting the truth as an
obligation of oath could be. This is the reason the
Court also insists that the dying declaration should be
of such a nature as to inspire full confidence of the
Court in its correctness. The Hon'ble Supreme Court
further held, to be on guard that the statement of the
deceased was not as a result of either tutoring, or
prompting or a product of imagination. The Court must
be further satisfied that the deceased was in a fit
state of mind after a clear opportunity to observe and
identify the assailant. Once the Court is satisfied that
the declaration was true and voluntary, undoubtedly,
it can base its conviction without any further
corroboration. It cannot be laid down as an absolute
rule of law that the dying declaration cannot form the
sole basis of conviction unless it is corroborated. The
rule requiring corroboration is merely a rule of
prudence. Thus on the basis of such judgment, this

10
Court is of the opinion that while basing on conviction
or overturn an acquittal recorded by the learned Trial
Judge, the Appellate Court must be satisfied that the
dying declaration was true and voluntary and it has
not been made as a result of tutoring, prompting or
imagination and that the deceased, at the time of
making the dying declaration was in a fit state of
mind to give the declaration.
14. In this case, we have very carefully examined the
contents of the F.I.R., the statement of PW 1 and 5
taken together with the statement of PW - 3 and we
find that there is some subtle variance between
them. Though, there are no contradictions but F.I.R.
is at a variance, in the sense that in the F.I.R it is
mentioned that she allegedly stated before the PW 1
and 5 that Teetu called her backside of her house in
the agriculture field and showed her a bottle and
stated that both of them should drink the same and
die.

11
15. Thus, in a case based on oral dying declaration, the
Court has to be very careful in examining the
materials available on record and only when the
evidence is of a sterling quality the judgment of
acquittal recorded by the learned Trial Judge should
be overturned by the Appellate Court. PW- 3 and 5
have also stated that immediately after making the
statement, she became unconscious, which creates
doubt as raised by the defence counsel, in this case.
16. It is stated by the PW-3 the brother of the deceased
that she made declaration before the doctor at
Himalayan hospital also, but such doctor has not
been examined, which also creates a doubt in the
case of the prosecution.
17. In this case also, there is no material available on
record to show that the deceased was in a fit mental
condition at the time of making the dying
declaration. Even the doctor at Himalayan Hospital,
who attended the deceased at the first instance, has
not been examined by the prosecution to throw some

12
light on the mental capacity of the deceased at that
time. After a very short period at hospital, she died.
18. In that view of the matter, this Court is of the
opinion that this case does not come within the
purview of the principles laid down by the Hon'ble
Supreme Court in the case of "Ghurey Lal Vs. State
of U.P. (2008) 10 SCC 450" for overturning the
judgment of acquittal recorded by the learned Trial
Judge.
19. The learned Trial Judge has the opportunity of
observing the demeanor of witnesses and such
opportunity and appreciation of evidence should not
be lightly interfered with by the Appellate Court.
20. This Court is also of the opinion that there are
certain discrepancies regarding seizure of the bottle
(containing poison) which was sent to the F.S.L. but
there are some evidence on record that there are two
bottles were found by the relations of the deceased.

13
21. In that view of the matter, there are no substantial
and compelling reasons to come to the conclusion
that the appreciation of evidence by the learned Trial
Judge was perverse or unreasonable requiring
interference with the same. Accordingly, the appeal
is dismissed.
T.C.Rs. be sent back.
(Alok Kumar Verma, J.) (Sanjaya Kumar Mishra, J.)
15.11.2022
(Grant urgent certified copy of this order, as per Rules)
